mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when GDP growth rate is high.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn causes the S&P 500 index to decline over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to decreased consumer spending and subsequently drives down the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the unemployment rate is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in economic activity, which leads to higher demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when industrial production is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts and GDP growth rate are increasing, it signals a strong demand for housing and a growing economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both housing starts and GDP growth rate are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2% and the CPI is increasing, it signals an expansionary monetary policy and increasing inflation, leading to higher borrowing and spending, which in turn causes the S&P 500 index to rise over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate is below 2% and the CPI is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales are increasing and the GDP growth rate is high, it signals a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month and GDPC1 > 2%
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when retail sales are increasing and the GDP growth rate is high.
